newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM says to name finance minister by Friday.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM says to name finance minister by Friday.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Thursday he would name a new finance minister to replace Amnuay Viravan on Friday to oversee the troubled national economy.
He did not name any prospective candidates. Amnuay quit on Thursday over differences with political rivals in Chavalit's six-party coalition government.

Chavalit also told a news conference that there would be no change in the current policy of defending the baht against speculative attacks and that finance and foreign exchange stability were his government's top priority.
"First, I will name an acting finance minister. And I will continue to monitor the finance ministry and will do so more closely as it is essential," he said.

"The important thing is that we will carry out measures that have been started, especially in the policy of fixing the baht where there will not be any change. And the new finance minister will continue this policy," he said.
Chavalit also appealed for more time to tackle Thailand's growing economic problems and said he would retain Amnuay's finance and economic policies.

"In order not to leave a long vacuum, we would try to wrap up our consideration (of a new finance minister) today. And tomorrow, we should be blessed with an auspicious occasion for an audience with the King for his appointment of a new finance minister," Chavalit said.
"All the steps and measures taken by Amnuay will be fully retained as they are quite close to producing results as each day passes," he added.

During his seven-month tenure, Amnuay launched a series of hefty budget-cutting and state-led rescue packages for the ailing finance and property sectors to solve the nation's financial and economic woes.

"On the issue of helping the finance sector improving efficiency and of assisting businesses in different fields deal with the current situation, the government will continue its best efforts to take care of them," he pledged.
Chavalit said key issues for the country were the state of financial institutions. The Thai finance sector is suffering under the weight of heavy loan exposure to the depressed property sector.
He said he had met senior central bank officials and there would be no changes at the Bank of Thailand.

Chavalit said: "I would like to say that for the past five to six days, although there have been changes in those charged with carrying out policies, the policies themselves do not change. In fact, those coming in to maintain these unchanged policies...will step up their joint efforts.

"The caretaker and the new finance minister will sustain the work left by their precedessor so as to quickly boost the economy and the finance sector. Specifically, on the foreign exchange policy, there will not be any change," he said.

The prime minister sought to calm jittery markets. "I would like to ask Thais and businessmen not to heed rumours or unfounded information that could cause panic in the financial and foreign exchange markets with all negative consequences to the country that we are all aware of."
Thai stocks ended sharply lower at a new 98-month low on Thursday on concern about the future of the government's economic policies following Amnuay's resignation, brokers said.
The composite SET index finished down 18.17 points, or 3.76 percent, at 464.77.
The Thai baht recovered against the dollar in late trade in offshore and domestic markets but dealers remained jittery of taking baht posititons, brokers said.
The baht strengthened to 25.845/25.945 to the dollar late in the domestic market from 25.920/26.050 in early trade.
In the offshore market, the baht was quoted at 25.000/25.400 late against 26.500/27.500 in the morning.
